Law Passed: Connecticut has no enacted packaging EPR law. Two consecutive packaging EPR bills have failed: HB 6917 (2025) passed the House 138-0 but died on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, and HB 5151 (2026), which would have required submission of proposals derived from Connecticut's waste characterization study including EPR recommendations, was introduced in February 2026 and died in committee.
Status Detail: Connecticut's 2025 bill (HB 6917, a solid-waste omnibus that included a mandate to study the need and viability of packaging EPR by January 15, 2027) advanced further than any prior packaging EPR measure but stalled in the Senate and never came to a vote. A follow-on 2026 bill (HB 5151) raised by the Environment Committee was also introduced in February 2026 and died in committee. Connecticut's 2026 legislative session has since concluded without passing any packaging EPR law or study mandate, and any future bill would need to be reintroduced in 2027.

Law Passed: No EPR packaging law has passed in Florida. The most relevant 2026 packaging bill, SB 240 (Auxiliary Containers), died in the Senate Appropriations Committee on Agriculture, Environment, and General Government on March 13, 2026, the last day of the 2026 legislative session. A companion preemption expansion bill, SB 766/HB 629, also failed. Florida retains its existing state preemption blocking local governments from regulating auxiliary containers (plastic bags, paper bags, and similar packaging materials), but no new statewide EPR or packaging reduction law was enacted.
Status Detail: Florida's 2026 legislative session ran January 13 to March 13, 2026 and ended without passing any EPR packaging legislation or packaging restriction bill. SB 240, which would have directed the Florida DEP to develop a uniform ordinance covering single-use nonrecyclable auxiliary containers (defined to include bags made of cloth, paper, plastic, foamed plastic, polystyrene, and similar materials), passed its first Senate committee unanimously in November 2025 but died in appropriations. Florida is not listed among any state currently active or pending on comprehensive EPR packaging by any tracked source as of September 2026.

Law Passed: Hawaii HB 750 (enacted as Act 103) signed into law May 27, 2025, requiring the Department of Health to conduct a statewide needs assessment for a potential EPR program covering packaging materials (including all packaging types) and paper products, with the assessment due to the legislature by December 31, 2027. Status Detail: Act 103 (HB 750) is active law: the Hawaii Department of Health began needs assessment work in July 2025 and is establishing an advisory council; the study is funded at $1.5 million per year for FY2026 and FY2027. Law Passed: Illinois has no enacted packaging EPR law. Status Detail: S673 and its Assembly companion A3744 — the 'Packaging and Paper Product Stewardship Act' — were re-filed on January 13, 2026 in the new 2026-2027 session and are currently referred to their respective environment committees; S614, a separate stewardship-plan-focused bill, was also introduced by Sen. Bob Smith at session start. New Jersey's two-year legislative session runs through 2027, making these bills eligible to carry over without re-introduction, and New Jersey is one of only two states (along with Virginia) whose EPR packaging bills are structured to carry over from 2026 into 2027. No floor votes have been scheduled and no passage has occurred.

Law Passed: New York Packaging Reduction and Recycling Infrastructure Act (PRRIA), SB 1464A / A1749A — failed to pass in the 2026 legislative session; bill remains pending with no enacted law.
Status Detail: The 2026 New York legislative session adjourned on or around June 5–6, 2026 without the Assembly voting on SB 1464A / A1749A, marking the third consecutive year the bill cleared the Senate but stalled in the Assembly. In April–May 2026, sponsors Sen. Pete Harckham and Assemblymember Deborah Glick introduced nearly 150 amendments to the bill to align it more closely with EPR frameworks in Minnesota and California, but Assembly Speaker Carl Heastie stated the bill lacked sufficient votes to pass. The bill covers all packaging materials — including plastic, paper, glass, cardboard, and metal — and would apply to producers with more than $5 million in annual net revenue responsible for more than two tons of annual packaging waste.

Law Passed: North Carolina HB 882, 'Break Free From Plastic & Forever Chemicals,' introduced April 9, 2025, is pending in the House Rules, Calendar, and Operations Committee with no further action taken.
Status Detail: HB 882 would establish an EPR program for packaging materials requiring producers to join a Producer Responsibility Organization and meet recycling and labeling requirements, ban toxic substances (including PFAS, phthalates, lead, and mercury) from packaging, and prohibit intentionally added PFAS in food containers. The bill was referred to the House Rules Committee on April 10, 2025, and has stalled there. An earlier version of the bill died in the same committee in 2023.

Law Passed: Oregon Plastic Pollution and Recycling Modernization Act (SB 582, 2021) is fully in effect. A federal constitutional challenge was defeated at trial on August 27, 2026, and full enforcement against all covered producers — including producers of all covered packaging materials — resumed immediately.
Status Detail: On August 27, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Oregon upheld the RMA in full after a five-day bench trial, rejecting dormant Commerce Clause and Due Process challenges brought by the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors (NAW v. Feldon), dissolving the February 2026 preliminary injunction that had shielded NAW members. A related class action (Lollicup USA v. Feldon, filed June 25, 2026) was stayed pending the NAW outcome, with a joint status report due September 10, 2026; that case may be dismissed in light of the ruling. DEQ's third RMA rulemaking (September 2025–early 2027) is ongoing and includes consideration of additional covered-product exemptions and covered material category changes; final proposed rules are expected before the Oregon Environmental Quality Commission in early 2027.

Status Detail: SB0269 was introduced January 23, 2025, amended in early 2026 to add small-business (under $10M revenue) and small-county (under 200,000 residents) opt-outs, passed the Senate Government Operations Committee 8-1 on March 11, 2026, but was then assigned to the General Subcommittee of the Senate Energy, Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee, where Republican co-sponsor Sen. Law Passed: Vermont S.139 (2025), a packaging EPR needs-assessment bill, was introduced April 2, 2025, referred to the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Energy, and did not advance out of committee. No packaging EPR law has been enacted in Vermont.
Status Detail: S.139 would have required the Vermont Agency of Natural Resources to complete a needs assessment on packaging management — covering reuse, recyclability, safety, toxicity, and quantity — and report findings to the legislature by January 15, 2027, with a $250,000 appropriation. The bill stalled in committee and did not pass. As of mid-2026, Vermont has no enacted comprehensive packaging EPR law and is categorized by the Sustainable Packaging Coalition as a state that 'could see a bill go all the way in 2027 or 2028.'

Law Passed: Virginia has at least one EPR packaging bill that remained active as of the 2026 legislative session and is among a small group of states whose bill(s) carry over into 2027 without needing full reintroduction. No EPR packaging law has been enacted. Governor Spanberger vetoed a separate producer stewardship bill (HB 86, mattress stewardship) in 2026, signaling scrutiny of producer-responsibility fee structures. The specific bill number(s) for the carryover packaging EPR legislation could not be confirmed from available sources.
Status Detail: Virginia is one of only two states — along with New Jersey — whose packaging EPR bill(s) carry over from the 2026 legislative session into 2027, meaning they do not require full reintroduction. No EPR packaging law has passed in Virginia. The 2026 General Assembly session produced significant environmental legislation overall, but packaging EPR did not advance to enactment, and the Governor's veto of a mattress stewardship bill on consumer-cost grounds underscores the political headwinds facing producer-responsibility legislation in the state.

Law Passed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act), signed into law May 17, 2025, establishing an EPR program for packaging and paper products including glass, plastic (all forms), paper, and metal packaging; now in active implementation phase with CAA designated as PRO.
Status Detail: The Recycling Reform Act (Chapter 70A.208 RCW) is in force (effective July 27, 2025). The July 1, 2026 deadline for producers to join or register with a PRO (Circular Action Alliance, designated March 4, 2026) has passed. Ecology published preliminary statewide collection lists for public comment August 5–19, 2026, and the PRO one-time payment to Ecology was due September 1, 2026. Rulemaking under chapter 173-950 WAC is underway, with full program implementation targeted for January 1, 2030.
